belief: Something is wrong with me because I don't look like others.
origins: Difference is often treated as deficiency, by media, peers, and sometimes medical language. Children especially take this in as fact about themselves.
teaches: God said, “Let Us make man in Our image” (Genesis 1:26). Every person is a unique image-bearer. “God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was very good.” “For You formed my inmost being; You knit me together in my mother’s womb.” “You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor.” Variation in the human family is part of creation. You are not wrong, and you do not have to match anyone.
self_statements: There must be something wrong with me.
I do not belong in the human family.
errors: Believing there is a right way to look and I do not match.
Predicting that I will always be seen as wrong.
Feeling different and concluding that I am wrong.
questions: Who taught me that different means wrong?
What does Scripture say God thought of what He made?
How can I speak kindly about my body?
What would I tell a child who looks like me?
truth: I am not wrong. I am made in God’s image and called very good. Variety is part of creation, and I can embrace who I am.
hw_truths: God called His creation very good.
I am made in God’s image.
I am crowned with glory and honor.
log: Each day, say one thing about yourself that is true and good.
actions: Write who taught you different is wrong.
Spend time with people who celebrate you.
prayer: Creator, You called what You made very good. Heal the hurt of being told I am wrong, and help me see myself as You do. Amen.
hw_questions: Who taught me that different means wrong?
What does Scripture say God thought of what He made?
How can I speak kindly about my body?
What would I tell a child who looks like me?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God called all He made very good.”
